# Documentation mirror synchronization

The site republishes a copy of each app's user documentation so visitors can
read it without access to the private source repository. The mirror lives in
`apps/docs/<app-id>/`, is generated by `scripts/sync-app-docs.mjs`, and is
governed by the allowlist in
[`apps/docs/sources.json`](../../../apps/docs/sources.json). Never edit a
mirrored Markdown file by hand: the next sync overwrites it, and a hand edit
hides what the source repository actually says. Fix the upstream document
instead, then sync.

## When to sync

- The upstream repository changed any allowlisted document, or added a
  user-facing document that belongs in the allowlist.
- A pull request that rewrites user-facing docs merged — in particular the
  zai-cli documentation and release pull requests, which move installation
  instructions onto the public one-line installers.
- `npm run validate:apps` reports that the recorded commit and the mirror
  disagree, or that files are missing or unlisted.
- A new app gains a `"documentation": true` catalog entry.

## How to sync

1. Make sure a checkout of the source repository exists and is up to date.
   Fetch read-only: `git -C <checkout> fetch origin <branch>`. Do not run
   `git config`, `git checkout`, or any writing command in a checkout you do
   not own.
2. Review the allowlist for the app in `apps/docs/sources.json`. Only
   user-facing documentation belongs in `include`. Keep contributor and agent
   material out: `.github/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md`, local-validation and testing runbooks, release
   engineering notes, and architecture documents that describe internals rather
   than how to use the app. Every entry removed from `include` belongs in
   `excluded` with a reason, so the next agent knows the decision was
   deliberate.
3. Run the sync from the site worktree:

   ```sh
   node scripts/sync-app-docs.mjs --repo <app-id>=<checkout> [--ref <app-id>=<git-ref>]
   ```

   The script reads the ref recorded in `sources.json` unless `--ref`
   overrides it, rewrites links between mirrored documents to the docs viewer,
   flattens links to documents that are not mirrored into plain text, copies
   referenced images, removes stale files, and records the source commit in
   both `sources.json` and `apps/docs/<app-id>/index.json`. Use `--check` to
   see pending changes without writing them.
4. Read the warnings it prints. A link that was flattened to plain text is
   usually fine, but a repeated warning about a document users clearly need is
   a signal to add that document to the allowlist.

## Privacy review (required before committing)

Read the full diff of every added or changed mirrored document. The script
fails the sync on a few known markers, but the review is yours, not the
script's. Look for and remove:

- Internal organization, team, or repository names — for example
  `shared-internal-tools`, `epi-platform`, or any other private repository
  slug.
- Internal hosts and endpoints: `*.visualstudio.com` organization URLs,
  `dev.azure.com/<real-org>`, corporate intranet hostnames, internal package
  feeds, or private CI links. Generic product names such as Azure DevOps,
  GitHub, or Microsoft Teams are fine; a URL that points at a specific private
  organization is not.
- Credentials of any kind: tokens, `ghp_`/`github_pat_` strings, connection
  strings, or example configurations containing real identifiers. Placeholders
  such as `dev.azure.com/example` are fine.
- Instructions that only work inside the private environment, such as
  installing from private release storage. Exclude the document and record why
  in `sources.json` until upstream rewrites it for public users.

If anything is ambiguous, ask the site owner before publishing. Publishing is
not reversible in practice.

## Finish

1. Run `npm run validate:apps` and `npm test`. Validation checks that the
   mirror matches its index exactly and that the recorded commits agree.
2. Check the rendered result at `/apps/docs/?id=<app-id>` with `npm start`:
   headings, tables, and code blocks should read correctly, and every remaining
   link should either open a mirrored document or a public URL.
3. Commit the mirror, the updated `sources.json`, and nothing else from the
   private repository.
